title: Egg-Free Polish Pierogi Fried
description: A malty, springy twist on the traditional Polish dish, made with English mustard and air-fried for a healthier take.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.notes: use a high-protein flour for best results

ingredients.name: warm water
ingredients.notes: not too hot, not too cold

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.notes: kosher or sea salt works best

instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine warm water, salt, and 1 cup of all-purpose flour to make the dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 equal parts and roll out each part into a thin sheet.
Use a round cookie cutter or the rim of a glass to cut out pierogi circles.
Place a tablespoon of potato-carrot-onion filling in the center of each pierogi circle.
Brush the edges of the pierogi with vegetable oil and fold the dough over to form a half-circle.
Press the edges together to seal the pierogi.
Dust the pierogi with unbleached all-purpose flour to prevent sticking.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in an air fryer at 375°F (190°C) for 5 minutes.
Add the pierogi to the air fryer in batches, not overcrowding the basket.
Cook the pierogi for 5-7 minutes on each side, until golden brown and crispy.
Serve the pierogi hot with a dollop of English mustard and a sprinkle of chopped fresh dill.
